title: Tone-curve table readback is accepted after two CPU reads with no GPU completion proof
source: Introduced by 630a6bf (PR #121); raised in the PR #121 review; fixed in a5cc71d.

expected.what: read_tone_table treats a recorded copy plus two equal CPU reads of the mapped READBACK buffer as a stable table. That proves nothing about GPU completion: the zeroed buffer before the first copy finishes, or a partly written table, is accepted.

table_exit records each copy into the simulator's command list at one fixed offset of a single buffer and counts it at record time with no fence or marker, so a later copy can overwrite the region being read.

evidence: The change copies the tone table into a process-lifetime READBACK buffer inside unfenced simulator recordings. The fix alternates two slots, writes a GPU marker per copy and reads only the slot whose marker is newest.
